q: How much power per tonne of ice do Bhimavaram's ice plants use?
title: Bhimavaram ice plants: kWh per tonne
short: 102 kWh per tonne on average. Bhimavaram's 80 block ice plants used 38.41 million kWh and 762 kL of diesel for about 376,000 t of ice a year. Plants observed ranged from 87 to 120 kWh per tonne; tube ice plants run at 55 to 65.
audience: Block ice plants in Bhimavaram, Akividu and nearby serving prawn and fish handling

ul: 80 plants making 90 to 130 kg blocks; 45 of them are 31 to 40 tonnes a day.
All use ammonia as refrigerant, so there are no HFC top-ups to count.
Electricity is 98% of energy; diesel runs generators during cuts.
Blocks take about 48 hours to freeze in brine tanks.

p: In the 31 to 40 tonne plants, compressor motors take 82% of the power, raw water pumps 9%, circulation pumps 7% and agitators 1%. So compressor running hours and the ice actually pulled decide your kWh per tonne. Part-loaded plants score worst.

ol: Take a month's units from the APEPDCL bill.
Count blocks pulled in the same days and multiply by block weight.
Divide kWh by tonnes. Above 110, check utilisation, brine tank insulation and compressor age.

p: The cluster manual costs a 15 tonne a day tube ice plant at Rs 24 lakh, saving 189,000 kWh a year against a block plant running at 90 kWh per tonne, with a payback of about 3.4 years. It suits buyers who crush block ice anyway.

example.title: Carbon per tonne of ice (estimate)
lines: Power: 102 kWh x 0.675 = 69 kg CO2 per tonne
Diesel: 762,220 litres x 2.645 kg / 376,000 t = 5.4 kg per tonne
Total about 74 kg CO2 per tonne of block ice
Tube ice at 60 kWh: 60 x 0.675 = 41 kg; 189,000 kWh saved = 128 t CO2 a year
example.note: From BEE's Bhimavaram ice making cluster manual; CO2 uses the CEA FY 2025-26 grid factor and Senseible's diesel factor.

senseible: The calculators turn your kWh and tonnes into a per tonne figure; Senseible can read the APEPDCL bills behind it each month.
